messages:
Ravi Patel: Quick thought — we should test two headline directions for the bench: 'Latency drives cost' vs 'Latency drives UX & retention'. which one do we push in the webinar teaser?
Lina Moreno: my vote is econ-first for the webinar audience. SaaS buyers care about $/MAU. UX angle better for product leads on demand gen.
Noah Kim: agree with Lina. we can A/B the landing page hero copy and route leads by which variant they hit. small experiment: 50/50 for first week.
Jules Tran: visual idea: a dual-axis chart where left y = median latency (ms), right y = $/1000 sessions, x = batching level (none -> aggressive). annotate the "sweet spot" where marginal latency cost per ms is minimal.
Ravi Patel: nice. also prepare a simplified bar chart for socials: three bars showing total compute cost for small/medium/large sessions. keep it readable on mobile.
Lina Moreno: social hooks draft (short):
- Variant A (econ): "Cut inference spend without sacrificing responsiveness — see how p50 maps to per-session cost."
- Variant B (ux): "Faster responses = happier users. Learn the latency levers modern teams use."
Noah Kim: add CTA tracking tags so Sales Ops can label leads: ?utm_campaign=bench_launch&utm_variant=A or B. Sales Ops: does that work for your routing?
Sales Ops: yep that looks good. we'll map utm_variant=A -> "cost-first" SDR queue, B -> "product-ux" SDR queue. please include workload toggles in form so we can qualify (chat vs embed vs search).
Jules Tran: measurements note for slide footnote:
```
model: community-13B
context: 1024 tokens
workload: conversational (avg 3 responses)
samples: 500k requests
metrics: p50, p95, tokens/session, est $/session (based on infra mix)
```
Ravi Patel: include a tiny callout about assumptions: GPU hrs price, batching settings, quant level. mark as "example workload" to be safe legally.
Lina Moreno: webinar flow idea: 15min bench story + 10min demo (show console routing + cost panel) + 20min Q&A. registration asks for company size and primary use-case so we can tailor follow-up.
Noah Kim: timeline: mock slides by Tue, landing page + A/B copy Wed, runway test live Thu, webinar on 2026-04-14.
marketing-bot: Reminder: Content deadline for paid promo is 2026-04-05.
Jules Tran: small creative ask — can the design team produce two thumbnail variants, one with dollar overlay and one with stopwatch? should map to the A/B variants.
Ravi Patel: sounds good. Lina — can you own social captions? Noah — you're on analytics for the A/B funnel. Jules — design brief to be sent today. Sales Ops — will you provide lead routing doc by EOD tomorrow?
Lina Moreno: yep will write captions and 3 alt headlines.
Noah Kim: I'll mock funnel events and conversion tracking.
Sales Ops: routing doc incoming by EOD tomorrow.
Ravi Patel: perfect. One more: include a one-line "ask" in the registration confirmation email: "Share a sample workload (optional) to get tailored benchmark notes" — that'll help prioritize demo slots. :thumbsup:
